reasons.A: Short, clipped sentences, imperatives and a brisk self-help tone; nothing of the passage's long, balanced periods or reflective hedging.
reasons.B: Closest sentence movement: long, evenly flowing sentences joined by semicolons and qualifying clauses, first-person plural with a quiet 'it seems to me' hedge, few short sentences, measured earnest tone.
reasons.C: Formal register and semicolons fit, and it opens on a question, but the impersonal 'one' replaces the passage's 'we/us', the stacked 'X; Y; Z' fragments and closing aphorism read as slightly overworked imitation.
reasons.D: Good stance match ('we', 'I think', 'I suspect', a closing question) and long periods, but interleaves short rhetorical sentences and anaphoric pairs ('Nothing... Everything...', 'Sometimes... Sometimes... Most often') the author does not use.
